P1.evidence: Setter notes were acknowledged but not read back - 'I already got some information from Derek, but I just like talking to people' - which loses the feel-seen effect the check is written for. The frame ran to two of four parts: 'See if it's a very great fit. If it is, we'll get you started. If not, I'll still point you in the best direction' plus 'where you're at, where you want to go.' Frame agreement and the open question were both clean.

P2.evidence: Weight and height asked directly; age was volunteered. Injuries handled properly and persistently - 'when did you have that accident?', 'now everything is good again, like, no injuries still?' and 'Any pains, pains or something we should know about, like with back or anything?' - and the rep came back to the accident later to establish the recovery timeline, which is what surfaced the nerve damage. Nutrition was excellent, down to protein grams, carbs and daily calories. Occupation was never asked and only emerged when the prospect used his Medicare clients as a motivation story. Health conditions and hereditary risk were not asked as such, and sleep and energy were not raised at all, on a call with a disclosed history of depression.

P3.evidence: The best Phase 3 in the batch. Mobility was raised early and specifically, the bridge question was put properly - 'why do you personally feel like now is the right time for you to take more action on this than you did before?' - and the future-self question was concrete and used the prospect's own material: 'when six months, 12 months from now, you walk through the neighborhood that's quite hilly and you're not getting exhausted... How would you then look at yourself?' The drive-through reached identity and legacy cleanly, with the Medicare-clients A-or-B frame doing the heaviest lifting, and the reflect-back was accurate and confirmed. The specific can't-do-it activity and the who-else question were both volunteered rather than asked for.

P4.evidence: Ran nearly complete and produced the most valuable material on the call. 'You had a personal trainer a couple of years ago right' opened it, 'what's the reason you're not just looking to get back with a personal trainer' surfaced the $6,000-then-$7,000 bait-and-switch and the loss of trust, and 'why did he not focus on training?' pinned the actual structural failure. The sustainability question was the best-formed root-cause question in the batch: 'what is it that we need to fix together in order to make sure it is actually sustainable for Alex and that you don't fall off after six or 12 months?' The scripted P4f line did not run, though the oxygen-mask reframe substituted for it reasonably given that this prospect's gap genuinely does include not knowing what to do.

P5.evidence: 'What if nothing changes and it stays the same?' produced the strongest consequence answer in the batch, entirely in the prospect's own words: 'if nothing changes, I'll have a heart attack. If nothing changes, I'll have a stroke.' The settle check followed and was confirmed. The why-not follow-up was not asked - the prospect supplied it - and the line in the sand was drawn by the prospect himself ('I'm tired of being in the gray zone, like, I need to be black and white about this') rather than by the rep.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran and landed hard: 'do you feel like when we get all of that in place, you're going to be able to get to the results...?' 'Yeah, absolutely. I trust the process.' A clear yes was obtained before price. But the second question - if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in - was never asked, and it is exactly the question that would have surfaced the partner and the funding before the number was named rather than four seconds after it.

P11.evidence: Only the $100 refundable deposit was collected, confirmed live by 'Invoice paid, download receipt'. No onboarding call with Trevor was booked - the meeting scheduled was a second sales call with the rep the following day. No agreement email and no signature. Partial credit on the last step: 'I will send you a link with an onboarding form. So you can get that filled out before we jump back on tomorrow... then he already has like all of the information that he needs.'

objection_plays.detail: The strongest run of this play in the batch. The isolate ran twice and cleanly - 'outside of wanting to talk about it, I understand... do you feel like it is going to be doable?' and later 'outside of finances, excited to get going?' Four of the six financial-picture questions were asked and answered: credit score (620), what is left after bills (a couple of hundred a month), credit card availability (almost maxed), and cash set aside (about $2,000). What did not run was the permission question, the SHOULD-I-versus-HOW reframe, the number and per-card limits, and any question about investments or other assets. The plan offered - three payments of $2,000 - was constructed after the picture rather than before, which is the right order.

'I have to go over that with my partner... I just can't spend the money without asking for it' landed within seconds of the price. The rep built rapport on it ('I've got a partner myself as well. I don't want to sleep on the couch either') and did establish that the partner was supportive, but that came from the prospect unprompted. None of the scripted moves ran - no 'what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason he would NOT want you healthier', no 'is this genuinely needing his input or asking permission to bet on yourself'. He went to the last-resort deposit move instead, which is now the second time in this batch that OB has been answered with a $100 deposit.

'Are you guys up for, I need a couple of days to think about it?' is a direct request and the rep granted it in one sentence: 'You can. We're not going to press you into doing anything, of course.' Not one scripted move ran - no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now', which is a line written almost exactly for a prospect who has just said he is tired of being in the grey zone.

Script gap on clinical fit, though this is the best-handled instance in the batch and partly because the prospect did the work himself. He disclosed eleven broken ribs, a punctured lung and a permanently denervated abdominal wall muscle, and volunteered that two doctors had cleared him with 'no restrictions on exercise'. The rep did probe the accident and the recovery timeline, which is more than happened on any other call. What is still missing is any step asking what activity was cleared, by whom, and whether loaded ballistic overhead work was contemplated - the clearance quoted came from a plastic surgeon discussing abdominal appearance.

notes: Technically the best-executed call in the batch: Phases 3, 4 and 5 all ran close to complete, the consequence frame produced the prospect's own words, and the money conversation was handled with more discipline than anywhere else in this rep's week. Two things to fix. He skipped the go-all-in question in Phase 6, which is the one move that would have surfaced the partner and the funding before the price landed. And when the think-about-it arrived he gave it away in a single sentence - the same reflex as on the Brian call. Worth a separate conversation with a manager: the financial picture he collected showed real distress, and the process has no rule about what to do when it does.
